subject.title: feat(agents): per-agent outbound A2A allowlist override

question: Should OpenClaw accept an outbound-only `agents.list[].tools.agentToAgent.allow` security boundary now, or wait for the broader per-agent session authorization model?
rationale: The patch changes public config, plugin SDK shape, and cross-agent session authorization semantics; automation cannot choose that security/product contract safely.

options.title: Hold for unified authorization review
options.body: Keep this PR open while maintainers reconcile outbound allowlists with per-agent session visibility, per-capability controls, and inbound access semantics.

options.title: Sponsor outbound-only A2A now
options.body: Approve this exact requester-owned allowlist model and require a refreshed branch plus upgrade/security proof before merge.

options.title: Close in favor of broader design
options.body: Close this PR if maintainers want all per-agent A2A/session scoping to land through the broader canonical issue and a replacement implementation.

recommendation.title: Hold for unified authorization review
recommendation.body: Keep this PR open while maintainers reconcile outbound allowlists with per-agent session visibility, per-capability controls, and inbound access semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant history points most strongly to prior session access/resolution and A2A allowlist work in the same authorization boundary.
